text: You’re allowed to wear a T-shirt with a candidate’s name on it while voting inside a California polling place.
seenIn: a friend’s Election Day outfit post

room.label: students (demo crowd)
room.note: No published poll has measured this belief yet. The 5C pilot survey replaces this split with real student answers.

truthSource.label: California Secretary of State: CC/ROV Memo #24196, Electioneering
truthSource.oneLine: Electioneering is banned within 100 feet of a polling place entrance, and it includes buttons, hats, shirts, or stickers with information about a candidate or measure on the ballot.

lesson.tip: The 100-foot electioneering ban covers shirts, buttons, and hats that name a candidate or measure on the ballot. General slogans aren’t covered. Ask: does it point to something on this ballot? If so, cover it up before you go in.
